## What I did

If DNA methylation is knocked completely out in the mutant line, TEs should have no chromatin accessibility bias because there should be equal accessibility of all. Should also be a lower rate of C to T deamination because of lack of methylation.

Look at the location frequencies of where the mutations occur across genomic regions. Ex. UTRs, centromeres, exons.

**Mariele's Mutation Spectra Project Suggestions (partially from chat):**

* `nucmer` or `minimap2` whole-genome alignment;
* `SyRI` (Synteny and Rearrangement Identifyer) for rearrangement and sequence-difference annotation;
    * [https://schneebergerlab.github.io/syri/](https://schneebergerlab.github.io/syri/) **( SyRI FINDS SYNTENIC DIFFERENCES)**
* `plotsr` for chromosome-scale synteny plots **(Plotsr VISUALIZES SYNTENIC DIFFERENCES FROM SyRI)**
    * [https://github.com/schneebergerlab/plotsr](https://github.com/schneebergerlab/plotsr)
    * Install with Conda (easiest)
    * Needs chromosome level assemblies (from minimap) for each of the genomes being compared and pairwise structural annotations between the genomes (Structural annotations can be gotten using SyRI)![Screenshot 2026-07-02 at 12.52.43 PM.png](data:image/png;base64,)
    * 
* perhaps `MUM&Co` as a second SV caller.
    * [https://github.com/SAMtoBAM/MUMandCo](https://github.com/SAMtoBAM/MUMandCo)
    * MUM&Co can call insertions, deletions, tandem duplications, inversions, and translocations larger than 50 bp from whole-genome alignments.
    * Outputs a TSV file with detected SVs
    * Can use BLAST to search for insertion/deletion events in reference/query to label as mobile or novel
* TE copy number by superfamily (identifiying what TEs are present and their copy numbers, which likely will be larger within the mutant line)
* mutant-specific insertions;
* WT-specific insertions;
* TE-associated deletions or rearrangements;
* insertion proximity to genes;
* enrichment in pericentromeres (in/near centromeres) versus chromosome arms.

Restrict SNP/indel analysis to confidently aligned, one-to-one syntenic sequence. (or could look at low reads to look at somatic mutation)

Then compare:

* six substitution classes;
* trinucleotide contexts (what nucleotides flank a SNP, can determine C-T transitions at CpG sites and look at mutation susceptability)
* indel length distributions;
* mutation-like differences at CG, CHG (C any nucleotide G sites,) and CHH sites;
* gene/intergenic and TE/non-TE partitioning.
